rejected.title: Layers of the Earth
card: Crust
The thin, rocky outer layer of the Earth. It is the layer we live on, and it is thinnest under the oceans.
Mantle
The thick layer under the crust. It is hot, solid rock, but it can flow very slowly over long periods of time.
Core
The centre of the Earth, made mostly of metal, mainly iron and nickel.
The crust and the very top of the mantle are cool and rigid. Together they are broken into large pieces called plates.
rejected.remember: Crust, mantle, core from the outside in. Plates are crust plus the top of the mantle.

a.q: Which layers make up the Earth's plates?
opts: The crust and the top of the mantle
The crust on its own
The mantle and the core
The crust and the whole mantle
a.why: The plates are made of the crust together with the cool, rigid top of the mantle. The crust on its own is tempting, but the plates reach down into the top of the mantle as well.
a.clue: Plates reach a little deeper than the crust, but not far.

b.q: A student says the Earth's plates float on a sea of liquid rock in the mantle. What is wrong with this idea?
opts: The mantle is solid rock, though it moves very slowly
The mantle is cold rock that cannot move at all
The plates sit on the core rather than the mantle
The mantle is made mostly of iron and nickel metal
b.why: The mantle is hot, solid rock that can flow very slowly over long periods, so it is not a liquid sea. Saying it cannot move at all is tempting, but the mantle does flow slowly. Iron and nickel make up the core, not the mantle.
b.clue: Think about whether mantle rock is solid or liquid.

a.q: Which part of the Earth is made up of the crust and the top of the mantle, broken into large pieces?
opts: The rigid plates
The core
The flowing mantle
The inner crust
a.why: The crust and the top of the mantle are rigid and are broken into pieces called plates. The flowing mantle is tempting, but it lies below the plates and moves very slowly, so it is not rigid.
a.clue: Think about which part is rigid and cracked into pieces.

b.q: Rock in the mantle is solid, yet it can slowly flow. A student says the plates must sit on a layer of liquid. Which statement is correct?
opts: The mantle is hot solid rock that flows very slowly
The mantle is a thin layer of runny liquid rock
The mantle is a layer of cold rock that cannot move
The mantle is made mostly of iron and nickel metal
b.why: The card says the mantle is solid rock that flows very slowly because it is hot. Calling it runny liquid is tempting because it can flow, but it is not liquid like water. Iron and nickel make up the core, not the mantle.
b.clue: Solid rock can still flow if it is hot and given enough time.

b.best: The mantle is hot solid rock that flows very slowly

a.q: A plate is one of the large pieces of the Earth's rigid outer shell. Which layers is a plate made of?
opts: The crust and the top of the mantle
The crust and the whole of the mantle
The mantle and the outer part of the core
Only the thin crust under land and sea

The mantle is cold, hard rock that cannot flow at all
The plates rest on the core, not on the mantle under them
The mantle is made mostly of the metals iron and nickel
b.why: The mantle is hot, solid rock that can flow very slowly over long periods, so it is not an ocean of melted rock. Saying it cannot flow at all is tempting, but the mantle does flow slowly. Iron and nickel make up the core, not the mantle.
b.clue: Is the rock under the plates solid or liquid?

a.best: The crust and the top of the mantle

b.best: The mantle is solid rock, though it can flow very slowly
